items.stem: Explain the term “G1 phase”.
items.answer: The interval between mitosis and the initiation of DNA replication, during which the cell is metabolically active and grows.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle and interphase is correct?
items.answer: Interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle.
items.markingKey: (a) Interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle. The other statements are false. DNA doubles (2C → 4C) but the chromosome number does not increase. options: Interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle.
Chromosome number doubles during S phase.

The M phase is the longest phase of the cell cycle.

items.stem: Describe the events of the four stages of mitosis with diagrams. Write the significance of mitosis.
items.answer: Prophase – condensation, centrosomes move to poles, nuclear envelope and nucleolus disappear; metaphase – chromosomes at the metaphase plate, spindle fibres attached to kinetochores; anaphase – centromeres split, chromatids move to opposite poles; telophase – nuclear envelope re-forms, chromosomes decondense. items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Synapsis occurs in zygotene; crossing over in pachytene.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Meiosis I is an equational division.
Reason (R): Diplotene can last for months or years in the oocytes of some vertebrates.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Meiosis I is reductional; meiosis II is equational. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between G1 phase and G0 (quiescent stage) on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A phase of the cell cycle is described: metabolically active. Identify the phase – G1 phase or G0 (quiescent stage)? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) G1 phase: between mitosis and the start of DNA replication; cell is metabolically active; cell grows continuously. G0 (quiescent stage): cells exit G1; metabolically active; do not proliferate unless required. (b) G0 (quiescent stage).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: G0 (quiescent stage); 1 mark: “metabolically active” is a feature of G0 (quiescent stage).

items.stem: A stage of mitosis shows these events: Golgi complex, ER, nucleolus and nuclear envelope disappear; spindle formation begins; chromosomal material condenses into compact chromosomes. Identify the stage. Give a reason.
items.answer: Prophase
items.markingKey: 1 mark: prophase; 1 mark: the features Golgi complex, ER, nucleolus and nuclear envelope disappear; spindle formation begins; chromosomal material condenses into compact chromosomes are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Mitosis is called an equational division.
Reason (R): The number of chromosomes in the daughter cells is the same as in the parent cell.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Chromosome number conserved.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “bivalent (tetrad)”.
items.answer: A complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Chromosome number doubles during S phase.
Reason (R): In a 24-hour human cell cycle, cell division proper lasts only about an hour.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: DNA doubles (2C → 4C) but the chromosome number does not increase. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A sub-stage of prophase I of meiosis shows: X-shaped chiasmata seen; homologues tend to separate except at crossovers. Identify the sub-stage. Give a reason.
items.answer: Diplotene
items.markingKey: 1 mark: diplotene; 1 mark: the features X-shaped chiasmata seen; homologues tend to separate except at crossovers are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between zygotene and diplotene on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A sub-stage of prophase I of meiosis shows: synaptonemal complex forms. Identify the sub-stage – zygotene or diplotene? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Zygotene: homologous chromosomes start pairing (synapsis); synaptonemal complex forms; bivalents or tetrads formed. Diplotene: synaptonemal complex dissolves; homologues tend to separate except at crossovers; X-shaped chiasmata seen. (b) Zygotene.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: zygotene; 1 mark: “synaptonemal complex forms” is a feature of zygotene.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Chromosomes are best studied at metaphase.
Reason (R): The nuclear envelope reappears in prophase.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The nuclear envelope disintegrates by the end of prophase and reassembles in telophase.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Give two differences between diplotene and pachytene.
items.answer: Diplotene: X-shaped chiasmata seen; may last months or years in oocytes. Pachytene: bivalents appear as tetrads; enzyme recombinase mediates exchange.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. diplotene – X-shaped chiasmata seen; may last months or years in oocytes; pachytene – bivalents appear as tetrads; enzyme recombinase mediates exchange.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about mitosis and its significance is correct?
items.answer: Mitosis results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement.
items.markingKey: (b) Mitosis results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement. The other statements are false. The nuclear envelope disintegrates by the end of prophase and reassembles in telophase. Chromatids separate in anaphase after the centromeres split. Mitosis is an equational division; meiosis is reductional.
options: Chromatids separate in metaphase.
Mitosis results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement.
Mitosis reduces the chromosome number by half.
The nuclear envelope reappears in prophase.

items.stem:
A phase of the cell cycle is described: cell grows continuously; between mitosis and the start of DNA replication; cell is metabolically active.
(i) Identify the phase. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were G0 (quiescent stage)? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) G1 phase (ii) DNA is not replicated (iii) cells exit G1; do not proliferate unless required
items.markingKey: (i) G1 phase – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: DNA is not replicated – 1 mark. (iii) for G0 (quiescent stage): cells exit G1; metabolically active; do not proliferate unless required – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Explain the term “cell cycle”.
items.answer: The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises other constituents and eventually divides into two daughter cells.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises other constituents and eventually divides into two daughter cells.

items.stem: A dog cell has 78 chromosomes (2n = 78). How many chromosomes are present in each cell after telophase I?
items.markingKey: (b) Each cell after telophase I: 39 chromosomes (counting centromeres).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle and interphase is correct?
items.answer: Interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle.
items.markingKey: (d) Interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle. The other statements are false. DNA doubles (2C → 4C) but the chromosome number does not increase. G0 cells remain metabolically active but do not proliferate unless called on to do so. It is a time of preparation: growth and DNA replication take place.
options: Cells in G0 are metabolically inactive.
Chromosome number doubles during S phase.
Interphase is called the resting phase because nothing happens.
Interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle.

items.stem: A stage of mitosis shows these events: nuclear envelope completely disintegrated; chromosomes condensed fully and seen clearly. Identify the stage.
items.answer: metaphase
items.markingKey: (b) Metaphase: nuclear envelope completely disintegrated; chromosomes condensed fully and seen clearly.
options: prophase
metaphase
anaphase
telophase

items.stem:
A stage of mitosis shows these events: nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER re-form; nuclear envelope develops around each cluster; two daughter nuclei formed.
(i) Identify the stage. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were anaphase? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Telophase (ii) chromosomes cluster at opposite poles and decondense (iii) centromeres lead, arms trail behind; daughter chromosomes move to opposite poles
items.markingKey: (i) telophase – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: chromosomes cluster at opposite poles and decondense – 1 mark. (iii) for anaphase: centromeres split; chromatids separate; daughter chromosomes move to opposite poles – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about meiosis and its significance is correct?
items.answer: In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres.
items.markingKey: (c) In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. The other statements are false. Crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. There is no DNA replication during interkinesis. Homologous chromosomes separate in anaphase I; sister chromatids separate in anaphase II.
options: Crossing over occurs between sister chromatids.
In anaphase I sister chromatids separate.
In anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres.
DNA replicates during interkinesis.

items.stem: Which term describes small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres that serve as sites of attachment of spindle fibres?
items.answer: kinetochores
items.markingKey: (b) Kinetochores: small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres that serve as sites of attachment of spindle fibres.
options: syncytium
kinetochores
metaphase plate
karyokinesis

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “DNA replicates during interkinesis.”
items.answer: There is no DNA replication during interkinesis.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: There is no DNA replication during interkinesis.

(a) Distinguish between G0 (quiescent stage) and S phase on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A phase of the cell cycle is described: cells exit G1. Identify the phase – G0 (quiescent stage) or S phase? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) G0 (quiescent stage): cells exit G1; metabolically active; do not proliferate unless required. S phase: DNA synthesis or replication occurs; DNA per cell doubles from 2C to 4C; chromosome number does not change. (b) G0 (quiescent stage).

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between leptotene and diplotene on any three points. (3 marks)

items.answer: (a) Leptotene: chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope; compaction of chromosomes continues; first sub-stage of prophase I. Diplotene: synaptonemal complex dissolves; homologues tend to separate except at crossovers; X-shaped chiasmata seen. (b) Leptotene.
